It has no internet permission, so it cannot upload, sync, track or show ads, whatever a future update might want. That is enforced by Android, not promised by a policy.

Still does not declare the INTERNET permission, so the process cannot open a socket. Your pictures cannot leave the device even if a library tried to send them. Check it on the Play listing without taking anyone\'s word for it.
Every export is measured after it is made, so the size and pixels you see are the file\'s own. Looks show the sliders they move. A picture that needed no change says so instead of pretending.
A tool you expected, a picture that came out wrong, a word in the wrong language: a message reaches a person.

Tap a tool to use it. One-picture tools ask for the picture first; batch tools open the steps with theirs switched on.
How Still works, in the order a first day goes. Nothing here needs an account, a login or a connection.

The big field on the home screen is the whole front door. Pick one picture and it opens in the editor; pick several and they go to the batch screen. Sharing from another app, or choosing Still from “edit in” or “open with”, lands in the same places. Every picture is copied privately first, so your original is never written to.

The strip under the picture is every panel: crop, square up, light, colour, curves, looks, detail, cut out, scan, draw, retouch, layers, frame, what is inside the file, and export. Hold the picture to see the original. Undo and redo keep a hundred steps. Auto on the Light panel reads the histogram and tells you which sliders it moved; a look is a set of slider moves you can see and change.

Add pictures, switch on steps, run. Resize, keep under a size, convert, enhance, a look or a saved recipe, watermark, frame, cut out, scan. The steps combine into one pass per picture. Hidden data is always removed; when that is the only step, a JPEG is cleaned byte for byte with nothing re-encoded, and its orientation is kept.

The red wash shows what will go before anything goes. Paint Keep over anything wrongly red and Remove over anything wrongly kept; the edge follows the picture’s own edges, so a short stroke usually does. Behind it: transparent, a colour, or a blur of the picture. Ink mode lifts a signature or a stamp off a photographed page. Export as PNG or WebP to keep transparency, or as a 512 × 512 sticker.

Square the page first on the Square panel. Scan then measures the light across the page and divides it out, so the paper goes white evenly and the ink keeps its weight. Colour keeps a stamp or a heading; black and white gives the smallest, clearest file.

Forms ask for a photo under 50 KB or 100 KB, sometimes at passport shape. Still finds the best quality that fits and only shrinks the picture if even the lowest quality is over, and tells you which it did. The number shown is measured on the file that was written.

Export prepares the file and shows its real size and pixels before anything is written. Save a copy makes a new file where you choose; the original stays exactly as it was. Share hands the file to another app. Settings can remember a folder so a batch is one gesture.

Still has no internet permission, so the process cannot send anything. Location is never copied into an export; camera fields only if you switch that on. A crash log, if there ever is one, stays on the phone until you choose to send it.
